goals: validation (stated): reproduce daily streamflow hydrograph at American River gauge and report NSE
mechanistic (prerequisite): characterize runoff + sub-surface drainage generation across the basin's elevation/soil/snow heterogeneity

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves per-point water partitioning and snow, but has no lateral transport or channel routing, so it cannot natively produce integrated gauge discharge.

answerable: per-column runoff (QOVER) and sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) generation across elevation/soil strata
snow accumulation/melt timing (H2OSNO, QSNOMELT) that sets the freshet
basin-summed area-weighted runoff vs gauge as a monthly/seasonal water-balance volume+timing check (NOT a routed daily NSE)

not_answerable.aspect: daily streamflow hydrograph and NSE at the American River gauge
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport, no channel routing, and no native integrated streamflow; columns are independent 1-D points, so summed runoff is not a routed daily discharge
not_answerable.needs: runoff routing / aggregation to gauge outlet

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soils), concentrated at hydrologically active zones
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands span the 1625 m relief and the rain-snow transition that governs freshet timing; crossing with ~2 dominant SSURGO textures per band gives ~8, plus light replication at the rain-snow transition (most hydrologically sensitive) = ~10. No validation columns can be pinned to the single integrated gauge, so N is driven purely by exploratory coverage.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample the 1200-1600 m rain-snow transition (controls snowmelt-driven hydrograph shape) and valley-bottom/riparian zones (where baseflow/drainage dominates recession). Sparser coverage on uniform mid-slopes.
sampling_strategy.replication: One extra column in the rain-snow transition band to capture soil-driven runoff/drainage spread where sensitivity is highest.

sampling_plan.reason: Captures baseflow-dominated drainage and recession behavior at the basin outlet elevation, spanning coarse vs fine soils.
Represents the bulk hillslope runoff generation between snow and valley zones across two soil textures.
Most sensitive band for freshet timing; oversampled across soils with replication to resolve snowmelt-driven runoff variability.
Captures peak SWE accumulation and late melt that time the spring hydrograph, spanning available soils.

validation_design.observation_source: USGS gauge: American River nr Nile (daily)
validation_design.comparison: aggregated — area-weighted sum of per-column QOVER+QDRAI vs gauge; feasible ONLY as a monthly/seasonal volume+timing water-balance check. Daily NSE requires routing and is NOT deliverable with the current stack.
validation_design.metric: volume bias and seasonal timing (proposed); daily NSE deferred until routing exists
validation_design.n_validation_points: 1 gauge (integrated outlet — cannot pin columns to it)

validation_design.target_variable: snow water equivalent (peak SWE / melt timing)
validation_design.observation_source: SNOTEL (if a station exists in/near basin — not listed in brief)
validation_design.comparison: analog — process check against nearby SNOTEL if identified; not co-located

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-varying), native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start + spin-up for baseflow

requires_capabilities.capability: runoff routing / aggregation to gauge outlet
requires_capabilities.why: convert independent single-column runoff+drainage fluxes into an integrated daily discharge at the American River gauge
requires_capabilities.blocks: the entire stated deliverable — daily hydrograph reproduction and NSE

requires_capabilities.why: baseflow/recession depends on initialized water table and storage; cold-start columns give artifact drainage
requires_capabilities.blocks: realistic recession limb and baseflow contribution

requires_capabilities.why: elevation-driven precip/temperature and snow are the primary controls on this basin's hydrograph

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM/elevation + SSURGO soil sampling within HUC boundary
requires_capabilities.why: expander needs real rasters to place stratified columns
validate snow accumulation/melt that drives hydrograph timing

requires_capabilities.capability: USGS gauge daily-discharge ingest + basin-area/drainage-area lookup
requires_capabilities.why: needed to area-weight and compare aggregated runoff, and eventually compute NSE post-routing

assumptions: American River sub-basin lies within CONUS so NLDAS-2 elevation-varying forcing applies.
The gauge is an integrated basin outlet, not a point observation — no column can be co-located with it.
SSURGO provides at least two distinguishable dominant soil textures across the elevation bands.
User will accept a partial deliverable (runoff-generation characterization + water-balance check) given daily NSE is not achievable without routing.
open_questions: Is a routing/aggregation capability planned? Without it the stated NSE deliverable cannot be produced.
What is the drainage area upstream of the American River nr Nile gauge, to define the aggregation domain?
Is any SNOTEL station in or near the basin available for snow validation?
Would the user accept monthly volume/timing agreement as an interim metric instead of daily NSE?
